newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Baht not low enough for interest rates to fall-DMG.
newsitem.headline: Baht not low enough for interest rates to fall-DMG.

text.p: The Thai baht will have to fall further before the Bank of Thailand (BoT) can cut domestic interest rates, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG)'s Asia Pacific Economic Research Department said on Thursday.

"The BoT is already seeking to stabilise the currency which will prevent a short term fall in rates. Thus rates are likely to remain high in the coming months as the BoT stabilises the baht. Eventually the currency will fall further before the BoT can cut rates," DMG said in a report.

On Wednesday the BoT stunned Asia's financial markets by allowing a 'managed float' of the beleaguered currency. The move was accompanied by a two percentage point hike in the discount rate to 12.5 percent.
Following the float, the offshore baht plunged some 15 percent to a low of around 29 to the dollar. The onshore rate dropped to around 27.50.
At 0016 GMT the baht was quoted offshore at 29.10/60.
"The success of this move depends on the flexibility of the exchange rate the BoT eventually accepts," DMG said.
""In our view the BoT must reduce interest rates by around 500 basis points if they are to ensure a full (economic) recovery," DMG added.
DMG said the first currency crisis in Asia in over a decade is a clear negative for the region, given all countries will no longer be perceived as impregnable.
"Clearly the prospect of competitive devaluations comes to mind, although we doubt such an outcome can occur," the report said.
It said that Wednesday's decision by the Philippines to raise overnight rates to 24 percent shows the extent of investors' concerns.
"While we expect the peso to survive this will be at considerable cost to the economy: interest rate and exchange rate policy are becoming too restrictive," DMG said.
